rows.name: DICE_CANCEL_SIGKILL_SEC
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon.
cells.Values and default: Number of seconds, parsed with `float()`. Text that is not a number ends the daemon at startup with an error. Unset: 10 seconds. Empty: the daemon ends at startup with the error `DICE_CANCEL_SIGKILL_SEC must be a number`.
cells.Effect: Sets how long the Dice daemon waits before it sends `SIGKILL` to a cancelled submission that is still running. The wait starts at the first cancel request. Read once at startup. `0`, a negative number, `inf` or `nan` gives 10 seconds. A cancel from an LSF runner or after a lost lease waits at most 2 seconds. The wait also applies when the first process of a submission exits and others remain.

rows.name: DICE_DISABLE
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Read by: `dice`, `slice` and the wrappers (`bin/dice`, `bin/slice`, `bin/rinzler` and 1 more file)
cells.Set by: A person, by hand. The Slice test fixtures also set it.
cells.Values and default: Exactly `1` enables it. Any other text, for example `true`, is off. Unset: off. The Dice host configuration file `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` decides whether work goes through Dice.
cells.Effect: On a legacy host the wrappers and `bin/slice` start the work directly, with or without the variable. On a shared host the wrappers and `slice run`, `slice bench`, `slice calibrate` and `slice submit` refuse to run and exit with status 2. On every host the `bin/dice` commands `daemon`, `submit`, `queue` and `cancel` fail with exit status 1. With `--remote`, the wrappers and `bin/slice` exit with status 2 unless `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`. Outside tests, the Dice daemon removes it from the environment of the programs it starts.

rows.name: DICE_LABEL
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: A person, `slice submit`, or the Dice daemon.
cells.Values and default: Any text. Spaces around the text are removed. Text that is empty after that counts as unset. Unset: the label is `make <goals>` when `MAKECMDGOALS` is set. Otherwise `bin/slice` builds a label from its arguments or sends none.
cells.Effect: Sets the label of the submissions that `slice run`, `slice bench` and `slice submit` send to Dice. The Dice queue shows the label. `slice run` also records it in its state file. The option `--label` of `slice submit` takes priority. The wrappers always pass `--label`, and the variable does not change their label. `slice submit` and the Dice daemon also set it for the program that Dice starts.

rows.name: DICE_NUMA_SIZES
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon.
cells.Values and default: Positive integers separated by commas, one slot count per NUMA node in slot order, for example `4,4`. Parsed with `int`. The sum must equal the slot count of the server. Unset: the daemon derives the counts from `numa_nodes` in `config/resource-map.yaml`. If that fails, it treats the whole server as one NUMA node.
cells.Effect: Tells the Dice daemon how many slots each NUMA node has. The daemon first looks for free adjacent slots inside one NUMA node. It uses slots that cross NUMA nodes only when no such block is free. The daemon reads its own environment, once at startup. A value that does not parse, has a count below 1 slot, or has a wrong sum raises no error. The daemon then treats the whole server as one NUMA node and ignores `numa_nodes` of `config/resource-map.yaml`.

rows.name: DICE_DAEMON_CHILD
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Read by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, `rinzler_proxy`, the wrappers and `slice` (`src/system/system.cpp`, `bin/rinzler`, `bin/slice` and 2 more files)
cells.Set by: The Dice daemon. `bin/slice` passes it to child tests.
cells.Values and default: Exactly `1` means that the Dice daemon started the process. Any other text counts as unset. The text is compared, not parsed as a number. Unset: the process is not under a Dice grant. `rinzler` and `runtron` parse placement options without grant checks.
cells.Effect: `rinzler` and `runtron` check placement options such as `--instance`, `--devices` and `--numa` against the granted slots. They then need `DICE_SLOTS`, `DICE_GRANT_ID`, `DICE_GRANT_TOKEN` and a `SYSTEM_CONFIG` with `--instance`. With `DICE_SLOTS` on a shared host, the wrappers and `bin/slice` start the work without a new submission. Set by hand without a complete grant, it makes `rinzler` and `runtron` fail at startup. Under a grant, `--no-opt` does not stop the pinning of application threads to the granted cores. On a legacy host the wrappers remove it before they start `gen/rinzler` or `gen/runtron`.

The four Dice grant variables are read by `rinzler` and `runtron`, and they sit in section 2.2. The rule and the layout contradict each other. A developer who adds a fifth grant variable cannot tell which one to follow.

rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

rows.name: DICE_GRANT_TOKEN
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Read by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, `rinzler_proxy`, the wrappers and `slice` (`src/system/system.cpp`, `bin/rinzler`, `bin/slice` and 1 more file)
cells.Set by: The Dice daemon. `bin/slice` passes it to child tests.
cells.Values and default: Text that is not empty. It is random text that the Dice daemon creates for one grant. The readers do not parse it. Unset: `rinzler` and `runtron` do not read it unless `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1`. In that case they fail at startup with `Incomplete Dice grant environment`.
cells.Effect: Proves the grant to the Dice daemon. The wrappers and `bin/slice` send it with `DICE_GRANT_ID` in a `grant-check` request, and the daemon compares it with the stored token. `rinzler` and `runtron` only test that it is set and not empty. `bin/slice` leaves it out of the command line that it writes to test logs. The daemon accepts the check only from the started program, its process group or its descendants. Without it, the wrappers and `bin/slice` exit with status 2 inside a grant.

rows.name: DICE_SLOTS
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: The Dice daemon. Inside a grant, `bin/slice` sets it for each test.
cells.Values and default: Slot numbers joined by commas, for example `4,5,6,7`. `rinzler` and `runtron` reject spaces, empty items and ranges. The wrappers skip empty items. `bin/slice` also accepts ranges such as `4-7`. Unset: the process holds no Dice grant. `rinzler` and `runtron` fail at startup when `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1` and this variable is unset or empty.
cells.Effect: Names the slots that Dice granted to the process. `rinzler` and `runtron` derive their instance from the slots. `bin/slice` and the wrappers `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron` ask the Dice daemon to confirm the grant. `bin/slice run` then runs its tests only on these slots. Every reader except `bin/ci/bench_refresh_quiesce.py` uses it only when `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1`. `rinzler` and `runtron` need one unbroken run of slots that equals one `--instance` share. `SYSTEM_CONFIG` must hold the matching `--instance`. Without `mode: shared` in `/etc/positron/dice.yaml`, the wrappers start the program without the variable.

rows.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Read by: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.
cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `int()`. It is the process id of the LSF runner (`bin/dice-lsf-runner`, the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server). Unset: with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_START_JIFFIES` also unset, the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
cells.Effect: On a shared host the Dice daemon records the runner process as the owner of the submission. When that process is gone, the daemon cancels the submission. It sends `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after at most 2 seconds. When either lease variable is set, the daemon rejects the request unless both are integers, `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`, the pair matches a live process of the same user, and the client descends from that process. `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1` without the two lease variables is also rejected.

hints.problem: Rule 3. One sentence has 35 words and lists four conditions after "unless". The limit is 30 words. The same cell uses the idiom "is gone" (rule 1). Original phrase: "When either lease variable is set, the daemon rejects the request unless both are integers, `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`, the pair matches a live process of the same user, and the client descends from that process."
hints.suggested:
Replace the whole cell with: On a shared host the Dice daemon records the runner process as the owner of the submission. When that process no longer exists, the daemon cancels the submission. It sends `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after at most 2 seconds. When either lease variable is set, the daemon accepts the request only when all 4 conditions are true. Both lease variables are integers. `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`. The pair matches a live process of the same user. The client descends from that process. `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1` without the two lease variables is also rejected.
Changes in this cell, in order: "When either lease variable is set, the daemon rejects the request unless both are integers, `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`, the pair matches a live process of the same user, and the client descends from that process." -> "When either lease variable is set, the daemon accepts the request only when all 4 conditions are true. Both lease variables are integers. `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`. The pair matches a live process of the same user. The client descends from that process." | "When that process is gone, the daemon cancels the submission." -> "When that process no longer exists, the daemon cancels the submission."

hints.problem: Rule 1 (wrong noun). "It takes the name from the environment" is unclear. The daemon reads the variable, not a name. The row `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` says the same thing in plain words. Original phrase: "It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment."
hints.suggested: Replace the whole cell with: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It reads the variable from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.

rows.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_START_JIFFIES
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Read by: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.
cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `int()`. It is the start time of the LSF runner process in clock ticks counted from boot, from field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`. Unset: with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID` also unset, the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
cells.Effect: Together with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID` it identifies the LSF runner process that owns the submission. The Dice daemon compares it with the start time of that process id. A different start time counts as a lost lease, and the daemon cancels the submission. The daemon rejects a request with only one lease variable, with text that is not an integer, or without `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1`. A value of 0 clock ticks or less never matches a live process. The runner sets both only after it reads its own start time.

hints.problem: Rule 1 (wrong noun). "It takes the name from the environment" is unclear. The daemon reads the variable, not a name. The row `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` says the same thing in plain words. Original phrase: "It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment."
hints.suggested: Replace the whole cell with: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It reads the variable from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.

rows.name: DICE_LSF_RUNNING
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Read by: `bin/slice`, `bin/rinzler`, `bin/runtron`. The Dice daemon (`bin/dice`) reads it from the environment that a client sends with a submit request.
cells.Values and default: Only the exact text `1` counts. Any other text behaves like unset. Unset: the process counts as not started by `bin/dice-lsf-runner`.
cells.Effect: Marks a process that `bin/dice-lsf-runner` started inside an LSF job. With `--remote`, `bin/slice` and the wrappers `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron` do not submit to LSF again. They run locally. The wrappers reject an `--instance` option that differs from the `--instance` in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`. Without `--instance` in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`, only `--instance 0,1` is accepted. `bin/slice submit` applies this rule only with `mode: shared` in `/etc/positron/dice.yaml`. With busy FPGA cards, `bin/slice run` exits and tries no smaller slot range. The Dice daemon rejects a submit request with `1` and no `DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID`.

rows.name: DICE_LSF_TERMINAL_OUTPUT
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Values and default: Only the exact text `1` counts. Any other text behaves like unset. Unset: `bin/slice run` draws its live status block only when stderr is a terminal.
cells.Effect: `bin/slice run` draws its live status block with terminal control sequences even when stderr is not a terminal. `bin/dice-lsf-runner` removes an inherited value. It sets `1` when `bin/dice-lsf-submit` runs with `--wait` and its stdout is a terminal. Without the variable and without a terminal, `bin/slice run` under `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1` prints at most one progress line every 10 seconds.
